Header: Gibberella indica ( Fusarium udum ) Kunyala kwa Nandolo

Prevention: Try to plant in fields with no record of wilt
Plough the fields early to allow good soil solarisation
Rotate every 3 years with sorghum, tobacco or castor
Monitoring: Monitor plants on a weekly basis after germination
The first signs of the disease are wilting of the leaves and the leaves will turn yellow and evenyually dry and turn brown
A purple band develops on stem extending upwards from the base
Split the stem lengthwise to see if there is any streaking of the internal tissue.
The xylem tissue turns brown and later turns black
At the first signs of the disease carry out green direct control measures
Direct Control: Uproot and burn all wilted stems
Restrictions: Chemical control is not recommended as fungicides are infective against fusarium wilt.
The use of resistant varieties is the only effective control method
